reuse.why: Routes the five inline midpoint copies (app.ts x2, forecast, schedule-template, preview) through one new shared helper that reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, and updates the existing getScheduledAmount, but adds getExpectedAmount beside getScheduledAmount instead of extending the existing helper.

duplication.why: Removes the inline copies, but leaves two shared helpers (getExpectedAmount and getScheduledAmount) each with its own missing/number/range dispatch, and the API field uses the one that ignores the approximate rule.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the other schedule amount helpers and the API model only calls it; fine layering.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and the API field; four release notes for one cumulative change are a minor excess.

maintainability.why: One function decides the planned amount for server paths, but UI and API consumers go through getScheduledAmount which knows nothing about isapprox, so the rule silently differs by caller.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal computes expectedAmount with getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount) without the operator, bypassing getExpectedAmount, so approximate amounts are reported at the exact value.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts getExpectedAmount re-implements getScheduledAmount's null -> 0 / number -> itself / range -> getRangeAmount dispatch under a new name instead of one helper delegating to the other.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedAmount gained the op parameter and an isapprox branch in step 3; the API call site (api-models.ts) and the desktop-client getScheduledAmount callers stay on the older helper that lacks it.
